properties.title: NRC Report: Listed Haz Waste F037/F038 near Yorktown, VA
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 964749 - Medium Affected: LAND - Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERN REFINING YORKTOWN, INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 964749
Incident Time: 2011-01-14 16:45:00
Nearest City: Yorktown, VA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: LISTED HAZ WASTE F037/F038
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERN REFINING YORKTOWN, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 500 gallons
AN 18” DIAMETER SEWER BYPASS LINE RUPTURED WHILE FLUSHING WITH FIRE WATER, RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF F037/F038 SLUDGE AND CONTACT WATER. AN ESTIMATED 5 TO 10 POUNDS OF SOLIDS AND 500 GALLONS OF IMPACT WATER SPILLED ONTO THE ROADWAY AND ADJACENT EMBANKMENTS AND INTO THE STORM WATER DITCH. THE WATER WAS SHUT OFF AND SOLIDS CLEANED FROM THE ROAD. OIL DRY WAS DEPLOYED ON THE ROADWAY AND OIL ABSORBENT BLANKETS AND HAY BALES WERE PLACED IN THE DITCH TO CONTAIN THE VISIBLE OIL SHEEN. THE DITCH WAS THEN DEWATERED INTO A VACUUM TRUCK. THE RELEASE WAS FULLY CONTAINED ON SITE AND NO RELEASE TO NAVIGABLE WATERS OCCURRED. THE REMAINING STAINED SOILS WILL BE EXCAVATED AND PROPERLY DISPOSED.

BASED ON THE PIPELINE AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SAFETY ADMINISTRATION REGULATION IN 195.52(A)(3) THE EXPECTED COSTS OF THE THIS INCIDENT COULD MEET OR EXCEED $50,000. THEREFORE, THIS NOTIFICATION TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER IS BEING SUBMITTED.

properties.content:

Location2: EC SHOULTS NUMBER 1 WELL

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BASA RESOURCES
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 32.560312, -94.881273 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 840 gallon
Report DescriptionCALLER STATES APPROX. 20 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED FROM A WELLHEAD ONTO SOIL AND INTO A 2 PRIVATE PONDS ON 32 ACRES OF PRIVATE PROPERTY. SOME OF THE OIL DID MAKE IT INTO A CREEK. THIS INCIDENT OCCURRED IN APRIL 2024. THE SUSPECTED RESPONSIBLE PARTY CONDUCTED CLEAN UP THEMSELVES; HOWEVER THE POND WAS TESTED AFTERWARDS AND STILL HAD OVER 10,000 TPH IN IT. PRIVATE SOIL TESTING WAS ALSO DONE BY THE OWNER BECAUSE OF EVIDENCE OF FURTHER CONTAMINATION AND 2 OUT OF THE 3 TESTS RESULTED IN NUMBERS THAT EXCEED THE SAFE LIMITS OF TOTAL PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS. THIS WAS REPORTED TO THE TEXAS RAILROAD COMMISSION AND THEY WILL NOT ACKNOWLEDGE THE TESTING AND NO FURTHER CLEAN UP HAS BEEN COMPLETED. A ROTTEN VALVE ON THE WELLHEAD CAUSED THE RELEASE. A CLEAN UP ESTIMATE RECEIVED FROM AN ENVIRONMENTAL COMPANY WAS FOR $950,000.
